value: ABR thresholds fall (sensitivity rises) with increasing frequency across the 4 to 47.5 kHz stimulus range; the most sensitive frequency was not established
eye: ear (acoustic coupler at the left tragus), recorded as auditory brainstem response
method: auditory brainstem response to 5 ms tone pips at 4 to 47.5 kHz; thresholds from average audiograms (Fig. 2B)
conditions: Eight fat-tailed dunnarts aged 12 to 18 months; n per frequency 6 to 8; anaesthetised with ketamine 75 mg/kg and medetomidine 1 mg/kg intraperitoneally; ABR is an electrophysiological threshold, not a behavioural audiogram; 47.5 kHz was the highest frequency tested

source.authors: Garrett A, Lannigan V, Yates NJ, Rodger J, Mulders W
source.title: Physiological and anatomical investigation of the auditory brainstem in the Fat-tailed dunnart (Sminthopsis crassicaudata)

quote: Average thresholds (n = 6 − 8) depicted as audiograms (Fig. 2B) reveal the fat-tailed dunnart ABR is more sensitive (lower thresholds) with increasing frequency.
note: Same paper, next sentence: 'Currently however, it cannot be established whether 47.5 kHz is the most sensitive frequency or if ABR thresholds decline rapidly at higher frequencies.' So no upper hearing limit or best frequency is claimed. Threshold values in dB SPL are in Fig. 2B only, not in the text. No sense_hearing record for this species on main (grep by taxon and DOI). Licence: Crossref lists CC BY 4.0 and the PeerJ page states the Creative Commons Attribution License. Sentence read on two WebFetch passes of the page.

value: two ABR sensitivity peaks: 200 to 1200 Hz (amphibian papilla) and 2000 to 3000 Hz (basilar papilla)
eye: ear (electrode behind the tympanic membrane), recorded as auditory brainstem response
method: auditory brainstem response to 25 ms pure-tone bursts from 200 Hz to 6 kHz at levels from below threshold to 110 dB SPL in 10 dB steps
conditions: Three males of the eared comparison species (Fig. 2b, n = 3); lightly sedated with topical benzocaine gel for the whole recording; recording temperature not stated; ABR is an electrophysiological threshold and the papilla assignments are the authors' presumption ('presumably corresponding'); the two earless Brachycephalus species tested alongside responded only at 200 to 1200 Hz

source.authors: Goutte S, Mason MJ, Christensen-Dalsgaard J, Montealegre-Z F, Chivers BD, Sarria-S FA, Antoniazzi MM, Jared C, Almeida Sato L, Toledo LF
source.title: Evidence of auditory insensitivity to vocalization frequencies in two frogs

quote: Two sensitivity peaks were shown for I. parva, presumably corresponding to the sensitivity ranges of the AP (200–1200 Hz) and the BP (2000–3000 Hz; Fig. 2b).
